name: Vasya and a Tree
description: Vasya has a tree consisting of $$$n$$$ vertices with root in vertex $$$1$$$. At first all vertices has $$$0$$$ written on it. Let $$$d(i, j)$$$ be the distance between vertices $$$i$$$ and $$$j$$$, i.e. number of edges in the shortest path from $$$i$$$ to $$$j$$$. Also, let's denote $$$k$$$-subtree of vertex $$$x$$$ — set of vertices $$$y$$$ such that next two conditions are met: $$$x$$$ is the ancestor of $$$y$$$ (each vertex is the ancestor of itself); $$$d(x, y) \le k$$$. Vasya needs you to process $$$m$$$ queries. The $$$i$$$-th query is a triple $$$v_i$$$, $$$d_i$$$ and $$$x_i$$$. For each query Vasya adds value $$$x_i$$$ to each vertex from $$$d_i$$$-subtree of $$$v_i$$$. Report to Vasya all values, written on vertices of the tree after processing all queries.
input_specification: The first line contains single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 3 \cdot 10^5$$$) — number of vertices in the tree. Each of next $$$n - 1$$$ lines contains two integers $$$x$$$ and $$$y$$$ ($$$1 \le x, y \le n$$$) — edge between vertices $$$x$$$ and $$$y$$$. It is guarantied that given graph is a tree. Next line contains single integer $$$m$$$ ($$$1 \le m \le 3 \cdot 10^5$$$) — number of queries. Each of next $$$m$$$ lines contains three integers $$$v_i$$$, $$$d_i$$$, $$$x_i$$$ ($$$1 \le v_i \le n$$$, $$$0 \le d_i \le 10^9$$$, $$$1 \le x_i \le 10^9$$$) — description of the $$$i$$$-th query.
output_specification: Print $$$n$$$ integers. The $$$i$$$-th integers is the value, written in the $$$i$$$-th vertex after processing all queries.
approach_summary: Precompute 2^k ancestor jumps up[u][k] and node depths in O(N log N). Compute LCA and path aggregates in O(log N) per query.
